# Module reference

One section per file in `extras/`. [COMMANDS.md](COMMANDS.md) answers *what can I run*, [CONFIG.md](CONFIG.md) answers *what can I set*; this answers *what is this file, and do I need to care about it*.

Source: `NebulaOS-klipper-extensions` at `178a0c2`. **30 modules.**

## What each section shows

**Purpose** is the module's own header, kept whole. These authors explain their reasoning in the header, and summarising it would discard the part worth reading.

**Registers** are the G-code commands the module registers, from its own `register_command` calls. A command marked *replaces upstream* is registered after de-registering Klipper's own - it does **not** behave as stock Klipper, and anyone arriving from stock needs to know before debugging it.

**Reads** counts the configuration options; the options themselves are in [CONFIG.md](CONFIG.md).

**Tested by** lists every test file that names the module - not just a file called `test_<module>.py`, which misses the ones named after what they test rather than after the file. A module no test refers to is marked as such.

**Author** appears only for vendored modules and is read from [VENDORED.md](../../VENDORED.md), not inferred. Community-authored code is never presented here as NebulaOS's own work.

**Nothing here is hardware-verified.** Everything is read from source.

## The five modules no test refers to

`bl24c16f`, `calibrate_shaper_config`, `gcode_shell_command`, `motor_constants` and `virtual_pins` - **all five are vendored community modules**, and every module NebulaOS wrote is referred to by at least one test. That is a coherent position rather than an oversight: vendored code is carried unmodified, so a test here would be testing someone else's project.

It is worth stating because the opposite reading is available and wrong. These are not the risky untested corners of NebulaOS; they are the parts NebulaOS did not write.
